newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria says 97 wheat crop may be below forecast.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria says 97 wheat crop may be below forecast.

text.p: Bulgaria's agriculture ministry said on Tuesday the wheat harvest was proceeding on schedule but may be lower than initially expected due to bad weather last month.
"The ministry forecast wheat output of 2.4 million tonnes in May, but due to hailstorms and heavy rains last month the harvest may be lower," a ministry spokeswoman said.
She said it was too early to make new forecasts from the yields of wheat harvested so far as the harvest began only 10 days ago.
A ministry statement said 33,557 hectares of wheat and 168,289 ha of barley had been harvested so far, which amounted to 2.74 and 59 percent of sown areas.
Some 32,000 ha planted to wheat and barley and 16,000 ha planted to spring crops such as maize, sunflower and sugar beet were damaged by the storms, ministry data showed.
The spokeswoman said the ministry was in talks with several commercial banks, urging them to extend credits to private mills to enable them to buy grain.

"The banks are expected to extend one-year credits to private mills with three-month grace periods, and the state is to secure 260 billion levs to guarantee them through the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development," she said.
The spokeswoman said that under the grain balance approved in May the country needed to import 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat until next year's crop, but that figure could be increased.
Bulgaria suffered an acute grain shortage earlier this year following uncontrolled wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996.
